conviction_note: Scale is the option-implied 23.5% (40% ATM spread, so indicative) blended down toward the 14.6% median reaction to about 21%; the one lean with any weight is that the company's own raised FY guide implies H2 adjusted EBITDA of only $4.6-6.6M (FY $23-25M less H1 $18.45M) against $7.3M in H2 2025 and $7.8M underlying in Q2 alone, which leaves room for a beat-and-raise of the kind this name bought +40.8% in August, offset by Kimberly-Clark's North America read (retailer destocking, heavier promotion) and a disputed revenue bar, so p_up is only 54; impact_sum (+1.5) and the scaled number (+1.68) agree in sign and size.
bar: Disputed. Q3 revenue: $80.8M and EPS $0.00 (whisper $0.01) per Earnings Whispers preview 2026-10-28 (https://finviz.com/news/410949/honest-company-must-prove-its-raised-outlook-survives-a-costlier-second-half); Benzinga lists $77.4M revenue and $0.03 EPS (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HNST/earnings-forecasts). The same EW piece says FY revenue consensus ~$309M, BELOW the company's raised $319-325M guide (which includes ~$10M zero-margin apparel liquidation). Company bar for guidance (Aug 5 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530979/000162828026053315/honestcoq2-26exhibit991.htm): FY26 revenue $319-325M, organic growth 5-7%, adj. gross margin mid-40s, adj. EBITDA $23-25M. My own walk: Q3 2025 organic base $72.6M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1530979/000162828025049530/honestcoq3-25exhibit991.htm) x 1.06-1.07 = $77-78M organic, plus ~$3M apparel liquidation = ~$80-81M reported, i.e. the EW bar sits on the guide. Because the two estimate sources disagree, every finding resting on the quarterly revenue/EPS bar is capped small.

findings.finding: The company's own raised FY26 guide implies a very weak second half: adj. EBITDA guide $23-25M less H1 actual $18.45M (Q1 $3.95M + Q2 $14.5M incl. the $6.6M tariff refund) leaves $4.6-6.6M for H2, versus $7.3M in H2 2025 (Q3 $3.5M + Q4 $3.8M) on a 38% adj. gross margin and $7.8M underlying in Q2 2026 alone on a 43.8% underlying margin; even after the guided ~20% marketing step-up, a Q3 near $3.5-4.5M would put the year on track for the top of or above the range, setting up a second raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-05 guide raise (revenue, organic, margin and EBITDA all raised) bought +40.78%; 2026-05-06 reaffirm with accelerating organic growth +10.03%; 2025-11-05 EBITDA guide cut from $27-30M to $21-23M sold -29.39%. The guidance line is what this stock trades on, in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The Street's FY revenue consensus (~$309M per Earnings Whispers 2026-10-28) sits below the guide's low end, i.e. estimates are positioned for management to have overshot, not for a further raise; and the stock has given back about 27% of the post-August rally to $4.39. If the market were pricing a second raise, the stock would not be at the bottom of its post-earnings $4.46-6.01 range with consensus Q3 EPS at breakeven.
findings.independence: Same-document arithmetic plus the Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1530979/000162828025049530/honestcoq3-25exhibit991.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1530979/000162828026011624/honestcoq4-25exhibit991.htm). Counterweight, already netted in the size: management said on the Q2 call it would reinvest tariff-refund proceeds into marketing and that SG&A rises in H2 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/honest-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-05/), so part of the low H2 is deliberate spend, not sandbagging.

findings.finding: Kimberly-Clark's Q3 2026 release says its North America segment had volume +2.0% but organic only +0.4%, with ~130bp of unfavourable retailer year-over-year inventory movements and lower pricing from increased promotional activity — the same US retailers (Target, Walmart, Amazon, Costco) Honest ships to, in a quarter where Honest's diapers are already losing distribution at two large customers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Honest's sell-in vs consumption gap has mattered before: Q3 2025 revenue missed (organic -4.7%) and the stock fell -29.39%, in part on retailer and diaper weakness. No prior print where a KMB read-through was the stated driver.
findings.why_not_priced: KMB is a $40bn peer read by staples analysts, not by the few small-cap analysts on HNST; Q3 HNST revenue consensus ($80.8M EW) is on the guide and shows no destocking haircut. If priced, the HNST bar would have moved down after KMB's 2026-10-15 preliminary data.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Honest's own 10-Q says two large customers' diaper distribution losses will keep hurting diaper revenue (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530979/000162828026053323/hnst-20260630.htm), which points the same way on diapers but is already in the guide. Against it: Honest's wipes/personal care (75%+ of consumption) grew consumption 7.7% vs a 2.3% category in Q2, and KMB's own NA volume grew 2%.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q shows $11.9M of IEEPA tariff refunds received (claims began April 2026), $6.6M of it in cost of revenue, NO receivable booked for further refunds because of timing uncertainty, and a $4.2M accrued liability to third-party manufacturers; any further refunds received in Q3 would land as another unforecast gross-margin one-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print carried the $6.6M refund (~790bp of gross margin) inside a +40.78% reaction, but the company separated 'underlying' EBITDA and the stock traded on organic growth and the raised guide; refunds were said to be reinvested in marketing, so their path to the guide is weak.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus Q3 EPS of $0.00 does not look like it carries a refund; no receivable was booked, so models built off the 10-Q have nothing to put in. If priced, Q3 EPS estimates would sit above Q3 2025's $0.01.
findings.independence: Other importers' 10-Qs (FIGS, Ouster) report receiving outstanding refund balances after quarter end (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001816581/000162828026069640/oust-20260930.htm). No Honest-specific confirmation of Q3 receipts.

findings.finding: The $25M buyback was fully used by 2026-08-05 (5.6M shares at $3.35 average in H1, the rest after quarter end) and the company ended Q2 with $105.9M cash and no debt against a ~$470M market cap, so a new authorization at the Q3 print is plausible; none has been announced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $25M authorization was announced with the Q4 2025 print (2026-02-25), which rose +20.78% alongside the guide; not separable.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference from a completed program and the cash balance, not an announced event; no preview mentions it.
findings.independence: Cash and buyback figures also in the Q2 8-K exhibit (same filing set, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530979/000162828026053315/honestcoq2-26exhibit991.htm). Note H1 free cash flow of $35.3M was partly inventory timing that reverses (Earnings Whispers preview), which tempers it.

findings.finding: Street FY26 revenue consensus is about $309M against the company's raised $319-325M guide (Earnings Whispers, 2026-10-28), so a simple reaffirmation forces estimates up, while Q3 revenue consensus ($80.8M EW / $77.4M Benzinga) sits roughly on my guide-derived walk of ~$80-81M (Q3'25 organic base $72.6M x 1.06-1.07 + ~$3M apparel liquidation).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats on this name: Q2 2026 beat and raise +40.78%; Q3 2025 revenue miss vs IBES $99.4M -29.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: Capped small because the bar is disputed between two aggregators and the $309M may be a stale or apparel-excluded figure; if the market believed the guide, the FY consensus would already sit inside the range.
findings.independence: Benzinga estimates page (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HNST/earnings-forecasts) disagrees on Q3 level ($77.4M), so the two sources do not agree; shares the EW document with the guidance finding's why_not_priced.

findings.finding: Diaper revenue is guided to keep declining: the Q2 10-Q says distribution losses at two large customers 'will continue to negatively impact our diaper revenue', and management called diapers a structural drag now under 25% of consumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Diaper weakness was cited in the -29.39% (2025-11-05) and -17.26% (2025-08-06) reactions; in 2026 it was offset by wipes/personal care and the stock rose on all three prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is inside the guide the company gave. Filed small because the size of the Q3 diaper decline is not disclosed and the rest of the company (wipes +26% consumption, personal care) must outgrow it to hit 5-7% organic.
findings.independence: KMB's NA promotional commentary (finding 2) points the same way on diaper pricing.

lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed between Earnings Whispers $80.8M/$0.00 and Benzinga $77.4M/$0.03): the bar-dependent finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4; the guidance finding is sized against the company's own guide, so it stands at +1.5.
Rule 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the tariff-refund finding cut from +0.4 to +0.3 because management said refunds are reinvested in marketing, so there is little path to the guide.
Rule 5 (proxy vs company number): the Kimberly-Clark read-through cut from -0.8 to -0.6 because KMB's own NA volume grew 2% and Honest's own Q2 consumption beat the category; filed as a proxy.
Rule 8 (thin coverage, understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 20 to 21; the guidance finding is an inference, not a confirmed number, so its size was not raised.

Rules 1 and 7: the reaction history shows the guide line pays both ways (+40.8 / -29.4), the short (8.8%, ~7 days) shrinks no negative of size here; left the remaining sizes alone. Net sum unchanged at +1.5.
